### What feature or enhancement are you proposing?

We would like to contribute the OneRobotics A1 robot assets to the Genesis project.

OneRobotics A1 is a fixed-base robotic arm with seven revolute joints.

We propose including three robot configurations:

1. A1 right arm (7 DoF)
2. A1 left arm (7 DoF)
3. A1 bimanual robot with stand (14 DoF)

The contribution would include:
- Original URDF robot descriptions
- All referenced STL meshes
- Model and actuator metadata
- Asset provenance and license documentation

The complete assets are already publicly available under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) license.

Source repository: https://github.com/katazen/onerobot_h1

We propose organizing the assets under:genesis/assets/urdf/onerobotics_a1/

The initial contribution is intended to be asset-only.It does not require changes to Genesis physics APIs,new controllers, or reinforcement learning environments.

We would appreciate the maintainers' feedback on whether these assets are suitable for inclusion in the main Genesis repository.

### Motivation

As a Genesis user working with robotic manipulators,I would like to access the OneRobotics A1 robot models through a clearly organized and reproducible asset distribution.

Currently, the A1 models are available in the OneRobotics source repository, but they are not included in the Genesis asset collection.

Providing the robot assets in a consistent structure would simplify model discovery, asset management,and reuse for developers working with single-arm and bimanual robotic systems.

OneRobotics has already published a separate integration for the mjlab ecosystem: https://github.com/T1Amoo/onerobotics-a1-mjlab

That project demonstrates our approach to maintaining a reusable robot integration with explicit model provenance, package-relative assets, and licensing.

We would like to provide similarly well-documented robot assets for the Genesis ecosystem.

### Potential Benefit

The proposed contribution would provide the following benefits:

1. Broader robot model coverage

   Add a publicly available 7-DoF industrial-style robotic arm to the Genesis asset collection.

2. Multiple robot configurations

   Provide independent right-arm, left-arm,and complete bimanual configurations.

3. Reproducible asset provenance

   Preserve the original URDF files, STL meshes,source revision, and model metadata.

4. Clear licensing

   Include explicit CC BY 4.0 attribution and license documentation.

5. Reusability

   Provide a common model asset foundation that developers may use for simulation, manipulation,and future research without requiring Genesis-specific RL or control components.

### What is the expected outcome of the implementation work?

- [ ] Confirm with the Genesis maintainers whether an in-repository asset contribution is appropriate.

- [ ] Provide the OneRobotics A1 right-arm URDF and its eight referenced STL meshes.

- [ ] Provide the OneRobotics A1 left-arm URDF and its eight referenced STL meshes.

- [ ] Provide the complete A1 bimanual stand URDF and its seventeen referenced STL meshes.

- [ ] Preserve the original robot geometry,joint definitions, inertial parameters,and model metadata.

- [ ] Document the source repository and exact source revision.

- [ ] Include the CC BY 4.0 license and OneRobotics attribution.

- [ ] Confirm that model assets can be loaded with the supported Genesis URDF importer before considering the contribution complete.

- [ ] Follow the asset layout and hosting approach agreed upon with the maintainers.

### Additional information

Project:
OneRobotics A1

Company:
OneRobotics
http://www.onerobot.com/

Original robot assets:
https://github.com/katazen/onerobot_h1

Proposed source revision:
3db6f614c8443bd9396fcd9304cf64a519f98f2a

Existing mjlab integration:
https://github.com/T1Amoo/onerobotics-a1-mjlab

Asset license:
Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International(CC BY 4.0)

https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/

Proposed asset inventory:

- Right arm: 1 URDF and 8 STL meshes
- Left arm: 1 URDF and 8 STL meshes
- Bimanual stand: 1 URDF and 17 STL meshes

The STL assets occupy approximately 28.6 MiB before compression.

The independent-arm models and the bimanual stand model are based on distinct CAD revisions.

No grippers are included.

Known source-model limitations:

- The independent-arm Link7 mass and inertia retain temporary flange placeholder values.

- The bimanual URDF retains zero effort and velocity placeholders. Confirmed actuator information is available in model_parameters.yaml.

These limitations are documented in the source repository and will not be silently modified.

The existing mjlab project validates a separate right-arm MJCF integration. Its results should not be interpreted as Genesis-specific validation of the proposed URDF assets.

We would prefer to contribute the three robot configurations together, while remaining open to maintainers' recommendations regarding repository size, asset hosting, or a smaller initial contribution.

new_candidates.body:
Hi - a licence question on GR00T N1.7 EA, asked here because the model card points to the NVIDIA Open Model License but is silent on two cases we run into.

Context: we operate shared on-site GPU infrastructure for robot fleets. A customer building on N1.7 fine-tunes the model for their own robots and runs it on compute we operate. In some cases we may run the fine-tune for them on our GPUs, on their data, with the resulting weights deployed only on their fleet.

Two questions:

1. Do the Open Model License terms on the nvidia/GR00T-N1.7-3B card (commercial use permitted; licensee owns its Derivative Models, s2.4) apply in full to N1.7 EA, or does the "EA" label carry additional restrictions (for example research/evaluation only, or no redistribution of derivatives)? We have seen at least one community derivative repo bundle a LICENSE file with a non-commercial research/evaluation restriction and want to know whether that reflects EA terms or that repo's own choice.

2. Where a third party (us) performs the fine-tune on a customer's behalf and the customer deploys the resulting weights, is there anything in the OML or the EA terms that treats that differently from the customer fine-tuning themselves? Our reading of s2.4 is that derivative ownership follows whoever creates the derivative, and we want to make sure we set up the contract correctly.

Happy to be pointed at a canonical terms page if one exists for EA releases. Thanks.

new_candidates.body:
### Ticket Type

🐛 Bug Report (Something isn't working)

### Environment & System Info

```Shell
- lerobot: main @ b9cb121 (installed from source with uv pip install -e ".[dataset,diffusion,pusht,test]")
- Platform: Linux 6.8.12-1021-tegra aarch64 (NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor, JetPack 7.2.1)
- Python: 3.12.3
- torch: 2.11.0+cu130
- gymnasium: 1.4.0
- gym-pusht: 0.1.6
- cloudpickle: 3.1.2
```

(`lerobot-info` itself exits with an error on this machine. torchcodec is installed but cannot load because the system FFmpeg has no `libavdevice`, so I collected the versions by hand. That is a separate problem.)

### Description

With the default eval settings (`eval.batch_size=0`, which auto-sizes to >1, and `eval.use_async_envs=True`, `src/lerobot/configs/default.py:148,151`), `lerobot-eval --env.type=pusht` fails. There are two separate bugs. Fixing the first exposes the second.

**1. The forkserver workers never import the env package.**
`EnvConfig.create_envs` imports `gym_pusht` in the main process if `gym_pusht/PushT-v0` is not registered (`src/lerobot/envs/configs.py:96-109`). It then builds an `AsyncVectorEnv` with `context="forkserver"` (`configs.py:116`). Forkserver workers start from a fresh interpreter, so the parent's import doesn't apply to them. `_make_one` (`configs.py:111-112`) calls `gym.make("gym_pusht/PushT-v0")` in each worker, and gymnasium raises `NamespaceNotFound`. The parent only sees a `ConnectionResetError` while checking spaces.

**2. Probing for `task` / `task_description` shuts the async workers down.**
`PushTEnv` has neither attribute. `rollout()` checks for them through `check_env_attributes_and_types` → `_sub_env_has_attr` → `env.get_attr(attr)` (`src/lerobot/envs/utils.py:172-177`, called from `lerobot_eval.py:288`). It also uses `env.call("task_description")` / `env.call("task")` inside `try/except AttributeError` (`lerobot_eval.py:256`, `:299-304`). With `AsyncVectorEnv`, the `AttributeError` is raised inside each worker. Gymnasium's worker loop treats any exception as fatal: it reports the error, closes the env, and exits. The parent then sets the pipe to `None`. The `except` in lerobot catches the re-raised error, but the workers are already gone. The next `env.step()` (`lerobot_eval.py:325`) fails with `AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'send'`.

`SyncVectorEnv` (`--eval.batch_size=1`) is not affected by either bug.

### Context & Reproduction

The `lerobot/diffusion_pusht` checkpoint on the Hub still uses the old normalization format (#4047). `migrate_policy_normalization.py` currently fails on it (#4457, #4499, #4649). So I used a local copy, migrated with a one-line local workaround that converts `crop_shape` to a tuple. Bug 1 happens in `make_env`, before any policy inference, so the checkpoint doesn't matter for it.

```bash
lerobot-eval --policy.path=<local migrated diffusion_pusht> --env.type=pusht \
    --eval.n_episodes=4 --policy.device=cuda --output_dir=outputs/eval_before_fix
```

The resolved config shows `'batch_size': 4` and `'use_async_envs': True`. Exit code 1.

Smaller reproductions without a policy:

```python
# bug 1
from lerobot.envs.configs import PushtEnv

if __name__ == "__main__":
    vec = PushtEnv().create_envs(n_envs=2, use_async_envs=True)["pusht"][0]
    # -> NamespaceNotFound in both workers, ConnectionResetError in the parent
```

```python
# bug 2 (needs bug 1 fixed, or any AsyncVectorEnv whose sub-envs lack the attribute)
vec.reset(seed=0)
try:
    vec.call("task_description")
except AttributeError:
    pass                       # what rollout() does
vec.step(vec.action_space.sample())
# -> AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'send'
```

`AlohaEnv` uses the same default `create_envs`, so bug 1 likely affects it too. I did not test aloha (gym-aloha is not installed here).

### Relevant logs or stack trace

```Shell
# bug 1, from each worker:
  File ".../src/lerobot/envs/configs.py", line 112, in _make_one
    return gym.make(self.gym_id, disable_env_checker=self.disable_env_checker, **self.gym_kwargs)
gymnasium.error.NamespaceNotFound: Namespace gym_pusht not found. Have you installed the proper package for gym_pusht?
# parent:
  File ".../src/lerobot/envs/configs.py", line 120, in create_envs
    vec = env_cls(
  File ".../gymnasium/vector/async_vector_env.py", line 314, in __init__
    self._check_spaces()
ConnectionResetError: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer

# bug 2 (with bug 1 patched locally, --eval.batch_size=2):
UserWarning: ERROR: Received the following error from Worker-1 - Shutting it down
AttributeError: wrapper TimeLimit has no attribute 'task_description'
UserWarning: ERROR: Received the following error from Worker-0 - Shutting it down
UserWarning: ERROR: Raising the last exception back to the main process.
  File ".../src/lerobot/scripts/lerobot_eval.py", line 325, in rollout
    observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step(action_numpy)
AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'send'
```

### Checklist

- [x] I have searched existing tickets to ensure this isn't a duplicate.
- [x] I am using the latest version of the `main` branch.
- [ ] I have verified this is not an environment-specific problem.

I have only run this on one machine (aarch64 Linux). Neither bug depends on the platform: (1) comes from the forkserver start method and (2) from gymnasium's worker error handling. The regression tests in the linked PR use a mock env and don't touch any hardware.

I have a fix with regression tests ready and will open a PR referencing this issue. This report was drafted with AI assistance (Claude). The reproductions and logs above come from runs on the machine listed above.

new_candidates.body:
Follow-up to [#8107's contact-preparation discussion](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/pull/8107#discussion_r4195816336).

Solver initialization has two different contact-capacity dependencies:

- Standalone VBD with rigid-contact history needs collision-pipeline capacity before solver construction: persistent history is allocated at construction and must exist before CUDA graph capture.
- MJWarp/internal-contact paths discover their required capacity from the constructed solver. Matching and sorting buffers must grow coherently with that capacity.

#8107 handles VBD with a bounded early call to the existing contact initializer, reused later. Moving every solver to contacts-first initialization would not preserve the second dependency.

Can we clarify the contact-capacity/preparation contract so each solver declares its dependency without duplicate allocation or rebuilding resources referenced by a captured graph?

Relevant owners are `NewtonVBDManager._build_solver`, `NewtonManager._initialize_contacts`, and `NewtonMJWarpManager._initialize_contacts`. Coupled solvers retain ownership of their entry-local pipelines and reset lifecycle.

This design follow-up is distinct from [Newton #4532](https://github.com/newton-physics/newton/issues/4532), which concerns coupled history correspondence, and #7783, which concerns a specific sorting-capacity mismatch addressed in #8107.

A useful resolution should document capacity ownership/order, preserve disabled/default paths and solver-owned capacity discovery, keep repeated initialization idempotent, and prepare history/matching storage before capture. No universal contacts-first order or new abstraction is prescribed upfront.
new_candidates.title: [Newton] Clarify contact-capacity preparation across solver initialization

new_candidates.body:
### Description

We hit an **intermittent SIGSEGV of `move_group`** in a setup that issues repeated motion-plan requests to one long-lived `move_group` process. After capturing a core dump and running controlled N-run experiments, we traced it to a **use-after-free of the lazy goal-sampling thread** in `ompl_interface::ConstrainedGoalSampler`, amplified by an **exception path that returns a planning context with a still-running sampling thread to the context cache**. We believe this is a genuine, currently unfixed defect pair in moveit2 (verified against `main` as of 2026-10-12), and we'd like to report it with full analysis and a minimal reproduction.

**Defect 1 (root cause — destructor-order UAF).** `ConstrainedGoalSampler` derives from `ompl::base::GoalLazySamples` but **declares no destructor**. Per C++ destruction order, the derived class's members (`constraint_sampler_`, `work_state_` (a `moveit::core::RobotState` value member), `kinematic_constraint_set_`, …) are destroyed **first**, while the base-class `~GoalLazySamples()` — which calls `stopSampling()` and joins the sampling thread — runs **last**. If the goal object is destroyed while its sampling thread is still active, the thread's callback (which captures `this` and uses `work_state_` / `constraint_sampler_` / a raw `planning_context_` pointer) keeps touching already-freed members during the join window → use-after-free → SIGSEGV.

**Defect 2 (amplifier — exception path skips `stopSampling()`; the cached context can keep an active sampling thread).** With a planner **configured to enable informed sampling** (we reproduce with **RRTstar** and `informed_sampling: true` in its planner config — note that OMPL 1.7.0's RRTstar has `informed_sampling` **disabled by default**, so a stock RRTstar configuration never constructs the informed sampler and never reaches this throw) and a **lazy goal region that has sampled 0 states yet**, OMPL's `PathLengthDirectInfSampler` constructor **throws** ("There must be at least 1 start and and 1 goal state when the informed sampler is created."). `ModelBasedPlanningContext::solve()` has **zero try/catch in the entire file**, so stack unwinding skips `postSolve()` (which is the only place `stopSampling()` is called on the normal path). `PlanningPipeline::generatePlan()`'s `catch (std::exception&)` only logs and sets `active_ = false` — **no context cleanup**. The context is not "returned" to the cache after the failure — it was placed in `PlanningContextManager`'s cache **at creation time**; when the exception unwinds and the request side drops its shared-pointer reference, `use_count()` falls back to 1 and the cached context — whose sampling thread was never guaranteed to be stopped/joined — again satisfies the reuse condition. (The thread **may** still be active at that point; it can also end on its own — its exit conditions include reaching `max_goal_sampling_attempts` (default **1000**), finding a solution, or `!isSampling()` — so in practice it can stay alive for tens of seconds.) The **next request for the same group+planner** picks up the cached context, and `ModelBasedPlanningContext::clear()` calls `setGoal(ob::GoalPtr())` — destroying the previous lazy goal **while its sampling thread may still be alive** → Defect 1's race fires.

**Mechanism chain (one line).** RRTstar (informed sampling enabled) × constrained pose goal → OMPL informed-sampler throws at setup → `postSolve()` skipped (stop/join never guaranteed) → cached context may keep an active sampling thread → next same-planner request reuses the context → `clear()` destroys the live goal → derived members die before the base-class join → callback UAF → SIGSEGV.

The same destruction path also runs at **process teardown**. We recorded one exit-time crash after SIGTERM (details below); that record is weaker than the in-run cores — the round contained EST, RRTstar and PRM requests, and the preserved core for it is truncated, so it independently confirms only an exit-time Signal 11, not the same UAF stack.

### Your environment

- ROS 2 **Jazzy**, Ubuntu 24.04 (noble), x86_64, binary (apt) installation
- moveit2 **2.12.4** (`moveit-core 2.12.4-1noble.20260617.141537`)
- OMPL **1.7.0** (`ros-jazzy-ompl 1.7.0-2noble.20260225`)
- Kinematics: a third-party **numerical** IK solver plugin (TRAC-IK 2.0.2 in our runs; TRAC-IK is a numerical SQP-based solver, not an analytical one — the solver class does not affect the lifecycle-defect conclusion). The defect is **IK-plugin-independent** — the UAF is in moveit/OMPL code paths (constraint-sampler callbacks and the goal-sampling thread), not in plugin code; any group with a working kinematics solver exercises the same path.
- **Verified still unfixed on `main` (2026-10-12):** `constrained_goal_sampler.cpp/.hpp` on `main` are byte-identical to 2.12.4 (md5 `1c91814f…` / `5fbe4dce…`; no destructor, no `stopSampling()` anywhere in the file), `model_based_planning_context.cpp` on `main` still has **0** try/catch, and `PathLengthDirectInfSampler` still throws on 0 sampled goals (`ompl@main`, L87-91).

### Steps to reproduce

Minimal recipe (synthetic; no special robot required — any arm-type planning group with an IK solver plugin works; group size is irrelevant to the mechanism):

1. Launch `move_group` normally for your robot (single long-lived process serving consecutive requests).
2. Build a motion-plan request with:
   - a **constrained pose goal** for the group: position-only tolerance (a centimeter-class sphere), orientation unconstrained → this routes through `ConstrainedGoalSampler` / `GoalLazySamples` lazy goal sampling;
   - `planner_id: RRTstar` **with informed sampling explicitly enabled** in its planner config (`informed_sampling: true`) — this is required: OMPL 1.7.0's RRTstar defaults to `informed_sampling: false`, and without it `PathLengthDirectInfSampler` is never constructed and the trigger does not fire. We expect any planner configured to construct `PathLengthDirectInfSampler` at setup (BIT*, AIT*, etc.) to behave the same; untested;
   - any fixed, reachable target pose.
3. Send the **same request ~20 times in a loop** to the same `move_group` process (service or action — we used the `compute_plan` service).
   - Each request fails almost immediately (~0.01 s) with error code `-1`/`99999` and the OMPL exception `PathLengthDirectInfSampler: There must be at least 1 start and and 1 goal state when the informed sampler is created.` — because the lazy goal region has 0 sampled states at planner setup.
   - Behind the scenes, the exception path does not guarantee `stopSampling()`/join, so each such failure **may** leave a still-active goal-sampling thread inside the cached planning context (the thread can also end on its own — its exit conditions include reaching `max_goal_sampling_attempts` (default 1000) or finding a solution — so the leftover is a race window of variable lifetime, not a permanent leak).

**Expected:** `move_group` survives; at most the requests fail cleanly.
**Actual:** `move_group` dies with SIGSEGV at a random iteration. In our fast-loop experiment it crashed at **iteration 19, <1 minute** after start. Measured crash probability per context-reuse destruction event: **≈12% (3 crashes / 25 destruction races — small sample, wide confidence interval)**. All observed crashes occur exactly at "a cached context's previous lazy goal is destroyed while its sampling thread is alive" (reuse) or at process-teardown destruction — never during an isolated first request.

Useful contrasts (all verified):
- **EST / PRM / RRTConnect** with the same constrained pose goal: solve terminates normally (success or `TIMED_OUT`/`GOAL_STATE_INVALID` — non-exception paths), `postSolve()` runs, sampling is stopped, no crash.
- **Joint-space goals**: did not crash in our contrast runs — but this is an **empirical observation, not a structural bypass**: in this version `ModelBasedPlanningContext::constructGoal()` also wraps a selected `JointConstraintSampler` into a `ConstrainedGoalSampler` (same `GoalLazySamples` base), so joint goals expressed as joint constraints go through the same lazy-sampling machinery. Non-crash in a contrast run does not mean the defect is structurally avoided.
- **Fresh `move_group` per request** (no context reuse): 0/5 in-run crashes — but see the teardown note below.
- **Teardown variant (one record, partially confirmed):** the single exit-time crash we captured occurred when SIGTERM was sent after an isolated round that contained **EST, RRTstar and PRM** requests (including one failed RRTstar request). The preserved core for this event is **truncated** (crash-reporter limiting); it confirms only that the process died with Signal 11 during exit — it does **not** independently confirm the same UAF stack. The same-family attribution is inferred from the shared exit-time context/goal destruction path. I.e. even isolated usage should not assume a clean exit after such a failure, but this record is weaker evidence than the in-run cores.

### Core-dump evidence (dual stacks, same core, concurrent)

From the one preserved **full** core (373 MB; `gdb`, complete **27-thread** backtrace; exactly **one** goal-sampling thread existed in the whole process — the orphan). The separate teardown-time core mentioned below is a different, truncated capture — the two must not be conflated:

Crashing thread (the orphaned sampling thread of the *previous* request's goal):

```text
#0  moveit::core::... (unmapped address)          <-- SIGSEGV
#1  moveit::constraint_samplers::IKConstraintSampler::samplePose(...)
#2  moveit::constraint_samplers::IKConstraintSampler::sampleHelper(...)
#3  moveit::ompl_interface::ConstrainedGoalSampler::sampleUsingConstraintSampler(...)
#4  ompl::base::GoalLazySamples::goalSamplingThread()
```

Concurrently, the executor thread serving the *new* request was inside the join:

```text
#3  __pthread_clockjoin_ex (joining exactly the crashing thread)
#5  ompl::base::GoalLazySamples::stopSampling()
#6  ompl::base::GoalLazySamples::~GoalLazySamples()
#10 ompl::base::SimpleSetup::setGoal(...)          <-- setGoal(GoalPtr()) from clear()
#11 moveit::planner_interface::ModelBasedPlanningContext::clear()
#12 moveit::ompl_interface::PlanningContextManager::getPlanningContext(...)
#16 ...::computePlanService / PlanningPipeline::generatePlan (new request)
```

This is the destructor-order race frozen in one core: the joining thread is destroying the goal (new request reusing the cached context) while the goal's sampling thread dereferences freed members.

Two independent later reproductions (separate `move_group` processes, separate days' builds with identical library offsets) produced the same signature:
- one with the identical stack as above (frame-for-frame identical in-library offsets),
- one with the UAF surfacing deeper in the IK callback chain (`ConstrainedGoalSampler::stateValidityCallback → checkStateValidity` on a freed `RobotState`) — same mechanism, different freed-block reuse. Stack traces were emitted to the `move_group` log (backward-cpp symbolization); the system crash reporter was rate-limited for these two, stated honestly.

### Root-cause analysis (code references)

Line numbers refer to `main` @ 2026-10-12 (2.12.4 is structurally identical, ±few lines).

**Defect 1 — `ConstrainedGoalSampler` has no destructor:**
- `moveit_planners/ompl/ompl_interface/include/moveit/ompl_interface/detail/constrained_goal_sampler.hpp`: members `planning_context_` (raw pointer), `kinematic_constraint_set_`, `constraint_sampler_`, `default_sampler_`, `work_state_` (`moveit::core::RobotState` **value member**); **no destructor declared**.
- `moveit_planners/ompl/ompl_interface/src/detail/constrained_goal_sampler.cpp`: constructor ends with `startSampling()` (L74); **no `stopSampling()` anywhere in the file**; the sampling callback `sampleUsingConstraintSampler` (L96) captures `this` and uses `work_state_` / `constraint_sampler_` / `planning_context_`.
- OMPL `src/ompl/base/goals/src/GoalLazySamples.cpp`: `~GoalLazySamples()` (L57-59) calls `stopSampling()` (L73: terminate flag + `join`). Being the **base** destructor, it runs *after* all derived members are already destroyed — the window in which the thread touches freed memory.
- Contrast: other `GoalLazySamples` derivatives in moveit2 (e.g. `GoalSampleableRegionMux` users) and OMPL's own docs assume `stopSampling()` before destruction; the derived class here never guarantees it.

**Defect 2 — exception path skips stop-sampling and re-caches the live context:**
- OMPL `src/ompl/base/samplers/informed/src/PathLengthDirectInfSampler.cpp` L87-91: throws when `numGoals < 1` — i.e. whenever an informed planner is set up against a `GoalLazySamples` that hasn't sampled a single state yet (which is the normal state of affairs right after `setGoal`, since sampling is asynchronous).
- `moveit_planners/ompl/ompl_interface/src/model_based_planning_context.cpp`: `preSolve()` (L743) starts sampling; `solve(...)` (detailed-response overload, L803) calls `preSolve()` at L852 and `postSolve()` at L958; `postSolve()` (L756-758) is the **only** `stopSampling()` call site on the request path; **the file contains zero try/catch** — any throw between L852 and L958 leaks the running thread. The same unprotected pattern leaves a second dangling pointer: `solve()` registers a **local** `PlannerTerminationCondition` (`registerTerminationCondition`, e.g. L860 in the `solve(timeout, count)` overload; unregistered only at L863 on the normal path), so an exception leaves the member `ptc_` pointing at the destroyed local — later dereferenced by `terminate()` (`ptc_->terminate()`, L1036-1039).
- `moveit_ros/planning/planning_pipeline/src/planning_pipeline.cpp`: `generatePlan()` (L251) `catch (std::exception&)` (L353-357) logs, sets `active_ = false`, returns false — **no `stopSampling`, no context reset**.
- `moveit_planners/ompl/ompl_interface/src/planning_context_manager.cpp`: contexts are inserted into `cached_contexts_` **at creation** (L415-416) and become eligible for reuse whenever the request-side reference is dropped (`use_count() == 1`, L346-359) — the exception path included; no "return to cache" step is involved. A leftover sampling thread's lifetime is bounded only by `max_goal_sampling_attempts_ = 1000` (L260) / solution / stop flag — tens of seconds in practice, far longer than the inter-request gap in any busy system.
- `model_based_planning_context.cpp` `clear()` (L627-651): `setGoal(ob::GoalPtr())` at **L647** destroys the previous goal — the live-destruction trigger on reuse.

### Suggested fixes

- **Fix A (root cause, minimal — 4 lines):** give `ConstrainedGoalSampler` a destructor that stops sampling before members die:
  ```cpp
  // constrained_goal_sampler.hpp
  ~ConstrainedGoalSampler() override
  {
    stopSampling();  // join the goal-sampling thread before derived members are destroyed
  }
  ```
  `GoalLazySamples::stopSampling()` is idempotent (it nulls `samplingThread_` after joining), so the base destructor's second call is a no-op. This closes the window **confirmed here** — the derived-member destruction window of `ConstrainedGoalSampler` (members freed before the base-class join). It is **not**, by itself, a complete guarantee against all process-exit lifecycle risks: the sampling callback also dereferences `planning_context_`, a **raw pointer** to the parent context, whose lifetime Fix A does not manage (see the parent-context item under Fix B).
- **Fix B (exception safety + lifetime hardening):** make the request path exception-safe so neither an active sampling thread nor a dangling pointer can survive in the cached context: run `postSolve()` (or at least `stopSampling()`) on **all** exits of `ModelBasedPlanningContext::solve()` (try/catch or an RAII guard), and/or have `PlanningPipeline::generatePlan()`'s catch block reset/stop the context instead of only logging.
  - **Also protect `unregisterTerminationCondition()`:** `solve()` registers a *local* `PlannerTerminationCondition` (`ptc_ = &ptc`) before invoking the planner and unregisters it only on the normal path; if the invocation throws, the unregister is skipped and `ptc_` keeps pointing at the destroyed local — a dangling pointer that `terminate()` (`ptc_->terminate()`) would later dereference. The exception-safe path must unregister **before the local object is destroyed** (RAII guard).
  - **Parent-context teardown (process-exit surface):** `~ModelBasedPlanningContext` is currently empty, and the goal (with its possibly-running sampling thread) is released only late in member-destruction order, while the sampler callback holds `planning_context_` as a raw pointer — an exit-time destruction can therefore still race the sampling thread against a partially-destroyed context. The parent context's destructor (or context-manager teardown) should **stop goal sampling first**, before its other members die. This is also why Fix A must not be described as a complete guarantee for all process-exit lifecycle risks.
  (Note: open PR #3894 touches the same `generatePlan` failure paths for error-code propagation — Fix B should be coordinated/rebased with it.)
- **Fix C (trigger surface, moveit↔OMPL coordination):** avoid the throw entirely, e.g. pre-sample the first goal state (`goal->sample()`) before constructing the informed sampler / calling `planner->setup()`, or treat `PathLengthDirectInfSampler` construction failure as a recoverable "not informed yet" state. For context: the throw itself is documented OMPL behavior (sanity check at construction); we consider moveit2's missing exception safety (Fix B) the primary defect and Fix C a hardening of the trigger surface only — **Fix C cannot substitute for Fix A/B**: any other throw between `preSolve()` and `postSolve()` (or an exit-time teardown race) still reaches the same unprotected lifetime windows.
- **Verification suggestion:** ASAN/TSAN build + the loop recipe above with ≥25 context-reuse destructions (and a SIGTERM teardown after a failed RRTstar request) expecting zero crashes; our harness reproduced 3/25 pre-fix.

### Related upstream reports (limited search coverage; no duplicate found within it)

- ompl/ompl#1317 (open): "Segmentation fault in BIT* … under repeated planning requests" — same problem *area* (informed planner family + repeated requests + intermittent `move_group` segfault, `PathLengthDirectInfSampler` warning in logs), but the posted stack crashes inside `BITstar::publishSolution()/bestPathFromGoalToStart()` with no goal-sampling/join frames — a different mechanism as far as we can tell. Cross-referencing in case maintainers see a connection.
- ompl/ompl@`1a680130` (2016, "Fix races in GoalLazySamples"): fixed races *inside* the base class; our defect is the **derived-class destruction order** on the moveit2 side, which the base class cannot guard against.
- **Duplicate-check status (stated honestly):** we did **not** complete an exhaustive duplicate check. Within a limited GitHub text search of moveit2/OMPL issues+PRs (all states; keyword matrix incl. `ConstrainedGoalSampler`, `GoalLazySamples`, `goalSamplingThread`, `stopSampling`, `PathLengthDirectInfSampler`, orphan/UAF/sampling-thread-crash families; 2026-10-12, re-verified the same day via authenticated `gh` CLI) we found no existing report or fix PR for this defect pair. Known coverage limits: GitHub search indexes title/body/comment text only (keyword-free mentions inside code diffs are unreachable), and the legacy moveit1 repository was not searched. Nearest neighbors checked and judged different-family: ompl#1317 (above), ompl#165 (2013, closed — segfault inside `RRTstar::updateChildCosts`, no goal-sampling/destructor frames), ompl PR#1476 (py-bindings GIL deadlock). Please read this as "no duplicate found within the described coverage", not as a completed exhaustive check.

### Notes and limitations (stated honestly)

- Small sample: 3 crashes / 25 destruction-race events; the per-event probability (~12%) has a wide confidence interval.
- The freed heap block was not pinned at heap level (no ASAN build in our production-adjacent environment); the mechanism rests on the dual-stack core, byte-identical crash offsets across independent processes, source analysis, and the controlled N-run contrasts.
- Teardown crash observed once, after a round containing EST/RRTstar/PRM requests; that core is **truncated** (crash-reporter limiting), so it confirms only an exit-time Signal 11 and does not independently confirm the same UAF; whether every isolated-run teardown crashes is undetermined.
- Other informed planners (BIT*, AIT*, …) are presumed to share the trigger but were not tested.
- The duplicate check is limited-coverage, not exhaustive (see "Related upstream reports" above).

### Follow-up offer

We can provide a **sanitized minimal reproduction package** (generic robot configuration + driver scripts for the loop recipe above) subject to our internal release review, and we're happy to test candidate patches (Fix A/B/C) against our N-run harness. Thanks to the maintainers in advance.
